subject: general
question:
'Families increase savings to offset the increased government dissaving.'

Who among the following has given the above mentioned theory?
solution:
The correct answer is "**David Ricardo**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first step in understanding **economic rent** is forgetting what you currently think of as rent.
 
• Economic rent has nothing to do with the more traditional definition of rent, which is a **payment** in exchange for the use of something for a set period of time.
 
• **Economic rent** is what the owner pays for additional services above what is expected.
 
• International free trade relies heavily on the idea of comparative advantage.
 
• According to **David Ricardo's** theory of international trade, which is partly based on **Smith's** concept of labour specialisation, countries should concentrate on doing whatever they can do more efficiently and then exchange their surplus for items they can't produce efficiently

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Like many of his contemporaries, **David Ricardo** was not a qualified economist. Although he didn't study economics, he did go to school to become a stock trader.
 
• He didn't start thinking and writing about economics until after a successful career in the **financial markets**, when he read Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations.
 
• A family of moderate wealth gave birth to Ricardo in 1772; he was the third of seventeen children to be born into the family. Despite disowning David for choosing a non-Jewish spouse, David's father, a **rich stockbroker**, gave him the connections he needed to pursue a successful career.
 
• Ricardo built up his own riches and died at the age of **51**, leaving three of his own kids.
